subject.title: Cron sessions deliver hallucinated output instead of failing cleanly when tool calls fail

question: What should OpenClaw do by default for cron/unattended final assistant text when the run has failed tools, missing data, or no proof of claimed completion?
rationale: Current source and tests preserve delivery after non-fatal warnings, while changing that default can intentionally suppress scheduled messages and affects a security-sensitive unattended trust boundary.

options.title: Fail Closed For Cron Only
options.body: Make cron/unattended delivery suppress or mark final assistant text as failed when required tool evidence is missing or failed, without adding broad claim verification to core.

options.title: Keep Current Recovery Behavior
options.body: Leave final assistant text as a recovery path after non-fatal tool warnings and rely on plugins or operator policy for broader trust checks.

options.title: Add Opt-In Strict Mode
options.body: Preserve the current default but add an explicit strict cron finalization mode with focused tests and upgrade documentation.

recommendation.title: Fail Closed For Cron Only
recommendation.body: Make cron/unattended delivery suppress or mark final assistant text as failed when required tool evidence is missing or failed, without adding broad claim verification to core.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest combined history signal on the affected cron files and the related broad claim-verification product-boundary decision.
